strengths: The paper targets a practical and relatively underexplored problem: incorporating semantic organization and seam visibility into automatic UV parameterization rather than optimizing geometry alone.
The ambient-occlusion-guided seam formulation is intuitive, differentiable with respect to the UV mapping, and potentially easy to integrate into existing neural parameterization methods.
The manuscript includes informative qualitative visualizations, comparisons with learned, classical, and commercial systems, geometric metrics, runtime measurements, and several ablations.

The appendix provides useful descriptions of the network architecture, losses, and ShDF-based partitioning procedure; the limited reported results suggest improved seam exposure and competitive conformality.
weaknesses: The technical novelty is limited: the backbone is largely inherited from prior neural parameterization work, while the semantic branch combines established ShDF segmentation, independent per-part parameterization, and simple grid packing. The closest cited semantic- and visibility-aware methods are not included as experimental baselines.

The central semantic-alignment claim is unsupported. ShDF captures geometric thickness rather than semantic identity, partitions are computed independently per mesh, and row-major atlas placement provides no mechanism for aligning corresponding parts across shapes. No cross-shape correspondence, texture-transfer, editing, or generation experiment is presented.

The evaluation is inadequately specified and potentially biased. Dataset identities, test-set size, mesh statistics, selection protocol, and variability are absent. SAMesh predictions are treated as ground truth, and generic UV charts are evaluated by agreement with those pseudo-labels, which inherently penalizes valid non-semantic chart decompositions. Visibility is evaluated mainly by the same AO quantity optimized during training and on only a few illustrated meshes.

There is a consequential AO-convention contradiction: Eq. 4 and the plots define 0 as occluded and 1 as exposed, whereas the seam-loss discussion states the reverse and gives reasoning inconsistent with Eq. 7. The normalized loss can also be reduced by suppressing all seam memberships or adding many low-AO seam candidates, without directly controlling seam length, count, or retained visible seams.

Claims of an end-to-end differentiable, joint semantic-and-visibility framework are inaccurate or insufficiently explained: ShDF/GMM segmentation, graph cuts, connected-component processing, and packing are non-differentiable, separate models are optimized per part, and the combined variant reported in the tables is not methodologically defined.

Essential UV-quality evidence is missing, including flip, overlap/injectivity, seam-length, chart-count, and packing-efficiency measurements. Equiareality drops substantially relative to several baselines, contradicting claims that geometric degradation is minor. Equal scaling of independently normalized charts also does not guarantee consistent texel density across differently sized surface parts.

Reproducibility is weak: the claimed public-code URL is blank, and important choices such as the number of semantic parts, optimizer and iteration settings, AO sampling, loss weights, seam-softening parameters, post-processing thresholds, baseline configurations, and hardware are missing or incomplete.

weaknesses: The claimed semantic contribution is largely a composition of an existing Shape Diameter Function partitioner, an existing UV backbone, and elementary grid packing. The method does not establish cross-shape semantic alignment: partition labels and connected-component relabeling have no consistent meaning across objects, and row-major packing of arbitrary labels cannot place corresponding parts consistently. No texture-transfer or correspondence experiment tests this central claim.

The semantic evaluation is invalid as evidence of semantic correctness. SAMesh predictions are treated as ground truth without human annotations, and the paper does not explain how UV charts from baselines with different chart counts are converted into comparable labels. Hamming distance and Rand Index under these conditions can be misleading.

The ambient-occlusion convention is explicitly reversed in the seam-loss discussion: Equation 4 defines 1 as exposed and 0 as occluded, whereas the text following Equation 7 states the opposite and gives a mathematically reversed explanation. Although minimizing the displayed equation is consistent with Equation 4, this contradiction undermines the central method description.

The seam objective has unaddressed degeneracies and does not enforce valid seam topology, seam amount, or chart validity. Its normalized soft-mask formulation can reduce scores toward zero, especially through the epsilon term, and the UV-distance surrogate can identify distortion rather than actual seams. No overlap, flipped-triangle, bijectivity, seam-length, or chart-count results are reported.

The visibility evaluation largely measures the same AO quantity directly optimized by the method. AO is only a geometry-based proxy, not visibility under stated 'typical viewpoints and lighting'; there is no independent perceptual metric, controlled rendering study, or user evaluation. Dedicated visibility-aware methods cited in the related work are also omitted as baselines.

Reported distortion numbers contradict the claim that perceptual objectives do not noticeably harm geometry. For example, visibility-aware equiareality is 0.6093 versus 0.8934 for OptCuts, and semantic-aware equiareality is 0.6707 versus 0.9341 for xatlas. These are substantial gaps, not minor changes.

The equal-cell atlas construction does not provide the claimed consistent texel density: independently normalizing every part to a unit square and then applying the same scale gives similarly sized UV cells to parts with potentially very different surface areas.

The experimental protocol is severely underspecified: there is no named dataset, mesh count, train/test protocol, uncertainty, hardware, baseline configuration, or precise metric definition. Essential choices such as the number of semantic components, graph-cut weights, post-processing thresholds, optimizer, iterations, neighborhood size, and seam-softening parameters are absent. The claimed public-code URL is blank.
Overall, the limited novelty, internal technical inconsistencies, non-reproducibility, and fundamentally inadequate evaluation leave the main claims unsupported at a top-tier-conference standard.
